children: A key shift is occurring in the relationship between oil markets
and U.S. real yields, according to Stephane Deo, senior portfolio manager at Eleva Capital.
Until mid-September, the two were positively correlated, but since then, the correlation has turned negative.

image.alt: US real yield vs. oil price

children: Deo explained that the previous narrative held that higher oil
leads to inflation, which leads to interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, which turns into higher real yields.
The new narrative, he said, states that higher oil prices
now lead to growth fears, which in turn lead to lower real yields.
The shift comes amid a broader market recalibration, with corporate earnings from heavyweights like Meta Platforms
escalating capital expenditures with uncertain near-term return on investment, prompting a severe global tech selloff.
As equity investors actively de-risk, capital pulled from volatile tech equities is flocking directly into U.S. Treasuries
, triggering the largest flight to safety in the sovereign debt market in years.
This massive surge in Treasury buying has driven bond prices up, causing the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield
to plummet by nearly 0.20 percentage points in a single day on Thursday, collapsing back below the psychologically important 5% threshold.
The US10Y is currently down 1.7% in the past five days but has recovered around 0.8% at 5.00% on Friday.

title: The correlation between oil and the markets has turned negative amid the tech selloff – analyst
